title: Framework PR #42 OSV trusted-base interpreter and lock ABI mismatch during CPython 3.14 transition
title_de: Framework-PR #42: OSV-Trusted-Base-Interpreter- und Lock-ABI-Mismatch während der CPython-3.14-Umstellung
profile: Framework PR #42 hosted OSV trusted-base CPython 3.14 transition follow-up with an exact-SHA-bound CPython 3.13.14 missing-selector bridge
affected_symbols: pull-request-head / Materialize trusted base Python version
technical_claim: The OSV pull-request-head job intentionally installs the checked-out trusted base requirements-ci.lock, but the prior remediation selected the PR-head .python-version as its interpreter. For exact PR #42 head e0564d2, this combines the trusted base CP313-only PyYAML hash with CPython 3.14.6, so pip correctly rejects the CP314 wheel. This is a deterministic trusted-base interpreter/lock ABI mismatch, not an invalid CP314 tuple.
entry_point: GitHub Actions pull_request execution of .github/workflows/ci-security-osv.yml on Framework PR #42.
source_to_sink_or_broken_control: A bounded but untrusted HEAD_SHA:.python-version blob flowed into the private setup-python version file and selected the interpreter that runs python3 -m pip install against the trusted base checkout's requirements-ci.lock. The current base f73f8842f45318e2df8aff1d31855eeb7c20a22f has the CP313-only PyYAML hash. The mismatch produces an intentional pip hash rejection before the OSV scanner can perform its base/head manifest comparison.
attacker_prerequisites: A pull request changes or introduces a CPython baseline while its trusted base uses an ABI-specific hash lock for a different interpreter.
The OSV pull-request-head job retains its required trusted-base checkout and installs that base lock.
observed_behavior: Exact PR #42 head e0564d219980d62bc37162ac6c11641f289f1b71 fails OSV run 29956021487, job 89045175516, after hosted setup-python selects 3.14.6. Pip installs the trusted base lock, expects CP313 digest 0f29edc409a6392443abf94b9cf89ce99889a1dd5376d94316ae5145dfedd5d6, downloads the CP314 wheel, and correctly reports digest c458b6d084f9b935061bc36216e8a69a7e293a2f1e68bf956dcd9e6cbcd143f5 instead.
expected_behavior: The OSV PR-head job must select an interpreter ABI-compatible with the trusted base lock while preserving its trusted-base checkout, SHA validation, read-only permissions, bounded base/head manifest reads, and no-execution treatment of the PR head. Only exact trusted base f73f8842f45318e2df8aff1d31855eeb7c20a22f with its missing selector may use the bounded CPython 3.13.14 bridge; all other base/selector states, including a present selector for that base or a missing selector at any other base, must fail closed rather than inherit a generic fallback.
impact: The historical e056 exact head had a failed mandatory CI/security check and could not enter protected Framework master. Exact current PR head 2930e04e1558b5b10bdeb87a76abb077a2085566 passes the repaired OSV control and all current hosted PR checks. PR #42 was then normally merged as resulting Framework master 935cf14c676a24672be5c336e92cd13457cc35c8, whose exact-master GitHub Actions workflows completed successfully. The defect is verified and no longer a release blocker. This remains a control-availability and provenance-consistency finding, not a confirmed product exploit; installing the PR-head lock, loosening hash enforcement, or executing the PR head would weaken the security boundary.
preconditions: PR #42 head e0564d2 selects stable CPython 3.14.6 through the bounded PR-head temporary file.
The PR base revision f73f8842f45318e2df8aff1d31855eeb7c20a22f has no .python-version and its requirements-ci.lock accepts the CP313 PyYAML wheel digest only.
The pull-request-head job checks out github.event.pull_request.base.sha before installing requirements-ci.lock.

root_cause: The earlier PR #39 remediation correctly avoided checking out or executing PR-head code by treating its .python-version as bounded SHA-verified data. On current PR #42 head e0564d2, that data selects CPython 3.14.6 while the retained trusted base f73f8842f45318e2df8aff1d31855eeb7c20a22f still has a CP313-only requirements-ci.lock. The workflow therefore coupled the trusted-base lock installation to the PR-head interpreter rather than an exact trusted-base interpreter/lock pair.
proposed_remediation: Replace unconditional PR-head interpreter selection with the reported uncommitted exact-SHA-bound trusted-base bridge: only when the checked-out trusted base is f73f8842f45318e2df8aff1d31855eeb7c20a22f and its selector is missing, select reviewed CPython 3.13.14 for installing that base lock. Every other base/selector state, including a present selector for that base or a missing selector at a different base, must fail closed. Preserve trusted-base checkout, base/head SHA verification, read-only permissions, bounded data-only PR-head reads, manifest comparison, and the prohibition on PR-head checkout or execution. Do not install the PR-head lock, loosen hashes, add credentials, or use a generic version fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Only exact trusted base f73f8842f45318e2df8aff1d31855eeb7c20a22f with its missing selector selects the SHA-bound reviewed CPython 3.13.14 bridge for requirements-ci.lock installation; all other base/selector states, including a present selector for that base or a missing selector at any other base, fail closed.
The job continues to check out the trusted exact base, validates base and head SHAs, and compares bounded dependency manifests without checking out or executing untrusted PR code.
The PR-head CPython 3.14 transition remains data-only at the OSV boundary; neither the PR-head lock nor a generic fallback replaces the trusted-base pair.
